items.text: Rule status update: 'Proclamation further modifying scope of Canadian products subject to additional (Section 338) duties' passed its effective date (2026-10-30) and is now recorded as in force.
items.notes: Status change based on the effective date in the signed proclamation.

items.text: Rule status update: 'Proclamation establishing the Oval Office National Monument' passed its effective date (2026-11-05) and is now recorded as in force.
items.notes: Status change based on the effective date in the signed proclamation.

items.text: Trump confirmed new US strikes on Iranian air-defence systems on Qeshm Island but called them minor. He also said Washington is talking with Tehran and has made a lot of progress. Qatar's foreign ministry spokesman Majed al-Ansari pushed back on claims that the Qatari-mediated talks had failed. Iran says it will reopen Hormuz and resume talks only if sanctions are lifted, assets unfrozen, the port blockade ended and attacks guaranteed to stop, and Trump has rejected those terms. Separately, the State Department's Rewards for Justice programme offered up to $20m for information on Iran's nuclear programme.
items.notes: Al Jazeera dates the Qeshm strikes to Friday Nov 6 in one piece and to Nov 7 in another. Earlier Qeshm strikes on Nov 3 were already reported, so this is a new round. The article also includes analysis from Tehran-based analysts. Al Jazeera is Qatari state-funded, and Qatar is the mediator.

items.text: US Central Command set up Task Force Iron Gate, based in Tampa. It will block weapons, dual-use technology, sanctioned goods and illicit revenue moving across Iran's land borders and the Caspian Sea. CENTCOM commander Adm. Brad Cooper said it will reinforce the naval blockade. CENTCOM also said its aircraft disabled the St Kitts-flagged cargo ship M/V Huda in the Gulf of Oman after it ignored warnings. It said that since July it has redirected 147 vessels and disabled five.
items.notes: Based on CENTCOM statements reported by Al Jazeera and by ABC Australia (citing AP and Reuters). Al Jazeera wrote 'Saturday, 8 November', but Nov 8 is a Sunday, so the announcement was probably made Nov 7 US time.

items.text: Iran's Revolutionary Guard lifted its self-imposed 2,000 km limit on ballistic-missile range, ABC Australia reported, citing AP and Reuters. Iran is not known to have longer-range missiles yet. Iranian state media reported explosions on Qeshm Island and at Jask, Sirik and Bandar Abbas on Saturday evening, with the cause unclear. Iran's military said two more tankers hit mines after using what it called an unauthorised route through the strait.
items.outlet: ABC News (Australia), citing AP and Reuters
items.notes: The mine claims come from the IRGC and have not been independently verified. Iran also made mine claims on Nov 5-6, which were already reported.

items.text: By 5pm ET on Nov 6, AP showed Democrat Scott Colom leading Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith by 2,574 votes (467,930 to 465,356), up from 2,010 earlier that day. Early affidavit returns favour Colom heavily: Oktibbeha County's 503 affidavits went 401 to 96, and Lafayette's went about 69% to 29%. Rankin County, a Republican stronghold, will begin scanning affidavits on Nov 10 and has rejected about 20% of those processed so far. Hinds County, where Colom leads 79-19, has not released its affidavit count. Nov 10 is the deadline for mail ballots to arrive and for affidavit voters to show ID, and counties must certify by Nov 13.
items.notes: These are late Nov 6 figures. No new statewide totals dated Nov 7-8 were found. Democracy Docket is a pro-Democratic litigation outlet. NBC (via NewsCord) puts processed affidavits at 9,242 and outstanding mail ballots at 3,139. Mississippi has no automatic recount.

items.text: An independent New York Times analysis of Alaska's ranked-choice data suggests Mary Peltola will beat Sen. Dan Sullivan once the also-ran Daniel J. Sullivan is eliminated, because most of his voters ranked Peltola second. Roughly 20,000 early votes and 27,000 absentee ballots were still uncounted. Sullivan's campaign expects them counted by Nov 10, and says he needs about 49.5% of the remaining two-way vote. Peltola's campaign says she won about 56.6% of early in-person votes and 56.7% of mail ballots.
items.notes: Democracy Docket says the Elias Law Group, whose chair founded the site, represents Peltola's campaign. The NYT analysis itself was not opened. The ranked-choice tabulation is set for Nov 18 (already a watch item).

items.text: As of Saturday, AP had Democrats at 254 House seats and Republicans at 162, with 19 races uncalled. Among new calls, Democrat Nancy Lacore flipped South Carolina's 1st District (49.7% to 48.6%). Republicans held NY-21 (Anthony Constantino), CO-3 (Jeff Hurd), AZ-5 (Mark Lamb), AZ-8 (Abraham Hamadeh) and NC-8 (Mark Harris).
items.notes: Updates the Nov 6 tally of 253-157 with 25 uncalled. Decision Desk HQ, but not AP, has projected FL-26 for Mario Diaz-Balart.

items.text: Congress returns on Nov 9 for a lame-duck session under Republican control, which lasts until Jan 3. Government funding runs out Dec 11, so a spending bill or stopgap is needed, along with the annual NDAA. Outgoing Republican Rep. Thomas Massie plans to force a House vote on impeaching Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth over the Iran war, and WSB-TV suggests the GOP's midterm losses could win it more Republican support. Speaker Mike Johnson said the session's work is far from finished.
items.notes: Massie's privileged resolution has been pending since September, when GOP leaders cancelled votes (Newsweek). Roll Call reported on Oct 26 that Massie had promised a vote in the first week.

items.text: Potential buyers in Anthropic's IPO are now discussing valuations of $1.2-1.3tn, and some as low as $1.1tn, TokenPost reported, citing four people familiar with investor talks. That is below the $1.4-1.6tn investors had earlier suggested to bankers. The same sources doubt the roadshow can start the week of Nov 9 and still list in November. Anthropic has announced no delay, and its Nov 2 amended S-1 still has no price range, share count or dates.
items.notes: TokenPost is a smaller crypto and finance outlet relying on anonymous sources, so treat this with caution. Relevant to W-261027-01, which is not yet resolved.

items.text: Federal Judge Lewis Kaplan ordered New York City to comply with an ICE administrative subpoena for the names and birth dates of men in a Bronx homeless shelter. ICE has narrowed the request to residents accused of certain violent crimes and agreed to a special master. The parties have two weeks to propose a plan. Mayor Zohran Mamdani's office and Attorney General Letitia James say they are weighing an appeal, and the city had called the request a fishing expedition aimed at sanctuary laws.
items.notes: Published early on Nov 7 UTC. Right-leaning PJ Media covered the ruling approvingly, but that piece was not opened.

items.text: AAA's national average for regular gasoline fell to about $4.04 a gallon on Nov 7, from $4.10 on Nov 5. AAA's weekly update had already shown a 12-cent drop over the week, the second straight week of declines.
items.notes: The $4.0371 figure comes from AAA's site banner, not from a dated press release. No diesel figure was found.

items.text: Interior Minister Marcin Kierwiński said the Kraków attacker acted alone, held very radical, ultra-nationalist views and appears to have been fascinated by far-right ideologies, adding that this still needs to be verified. Right-wing media and politicians accused him of politicising the tragedy without evidence. TV Republika called it insinuation, and wPolityce ran headlines calling the remarks outrageous and saying foreign media were already using them. Centrist and liberal outlets (RMF24, Dziennik.pl, Reuters) reported the remarks as the minister's preliminary findings.
items.notes: Contested. The wPolityce articles could not be opened, so only their headlines were seen. Comes a day after Kierwiński survived a no-confidence vote.

items.text: At the same press conference, Kierwiński said holding the Nov 11 Independence March in Warsaw would be analysed in light of the attack. He said the services are on heightened alert because of other information he did not specify. A weapons ban (including unloaded guns) and a pyrotechnics ban were already in place for Nov 11 in Warsaw.
items.notes: Organisers expect up to 500,000 people and Nawrocki plans to attend. No decision to restrict the march had been reported as of Nov 8.

items.text: PiS leader Jarosław Kaczyński, through the party's spokesman, appealed for protests against the government's actions on the Constitutional Tribunal to be called off after the Kraków attack.
items.notes: The article did not say which protests or dates. Do Rzeczy carried a similar headline.

items.text: Seven prosecutors from three units, including the National Prosecutor's Office, are investigating the attack and whether anyone helped the attacker. ABW and military counterintelligence (SKW) are examining his background, contacts and possible foreign disinformation. He was a sport shooter at a club in Starachowice with two firearms registered in his name. Interia reports his father had 11 registered guns and owned the car used. No charges had been announced; the suspect is in critical but stable condition after several operations.
items.reporter: Łukasz Szpyrka, Dawid Serafin, Dagmara Pakuła
items.notes: Expect a debate on access to firearms and sport-shooting permits. Police rejected claims of a slow response, saying the first patrol acted 23 seconds after the call.

items.text: As of Sunday morning, the government's maximum fuel prices under the CPN programme were set only through Monday Nov 9 (6.12 zł/l for 95 petrol, 7.83 zł for diesel), and no caps for Nov 10 onward had been announced. Autogas (LPG), which is not capped, reached a record average of 4.03 zł/l according to Reflex. Analysts at e-petrol forecast petrol at 5.99–6.15 zł and diesel at 7.71–7.85 zł next week. NBP's latest projection assumes CPN ends at the end of 2026, and NBP economist Jacek Kotłowski said keeping it would lower 2027 inflation by 0.9 points.
items.notes: The headline promises prices after Nov 10, but the figures are forecasts, not official caps.

items.text: Ahead of the Nov 9–22 KOALICJA 26.2 exercise, Rzeszów News reports about 4,800 troops in total: some 2,800 from 10 allied countries plus nearly 2,000 Polish soldiers, based mainly at the Nowa Dęba range in Podkarpacie, with air elements in Romania and naval mine clearance. Britain is sending about 300 soldiers of the 7th Brigade, Eurofighter Typhoons and a Voyager tanker. The drill tests the Multinational Force Ukraine led by Britain's Gen. Tom Bateman. The Defence Ministry says Poland will provide logistics and has no plans to send troops to Ukraine.
items.notes: New compared with earlier reports: the Polish troop number and the UK contribution. French Defence Minister Vautrin is expected to attend. The milmag link was not opened.

items.text: Poland will give Ukraine an extra 8 million zł (about €1.8m) through the Energy Community to buy power generators before winter, FM Radosław Sikorski announced after the Council of the Baltic Sea States meeting in Warsaw. Sikorski said Ukraine must not be forced to negotiate under attacks on civilians, that no settlement can be imposed without Kyiv at the table, and that Poland is ready to take part in negotiations.
items.notes: Fills in the amount and channel missing from the Nov 6 PAP headline already reported.

items.text: A United Surveys poll for Wirtualna Polska (CATI, n=1,000, fieldwork Nov 2) puts KO at 27.2% (down 2.5 points), PiS at 18.2% (up 1), Konfederacja at 13.3% and Braun's Konfederacja Korony Polskiej at 11.6%. Lewica has 7.1%, Rozwój Plus 5.2%, Razem 3.8%, PSL 2.9% and Polska 2050 0%, with 10.7% undecided. Interia links KO's drop to the Constitutional Tribunal crisis. A seat projection using Prof. Flis's calculator gives KO 172, PiS 108, Konfederacja 73 and KKP 61.
items.notes: The exact publication date is unclear; it was cached on Nov 7. Contrast with the CBOS poll (fieldwork Nov 2–4), which had PiS falling.

items.text: President Nawrocki appointed four NBP management board members, ending an eight-month standoff after Tusk countersigned the nominations. Marta Kightley becomes first deputy president. MPC members Ludwik Kotecki, Przemysław Litwiniuk (also a deputy president) and Marcin Zarzecki (from Jan 2, 2027) join the board. Because three of them leave the Monetary Policy Council, it will need three new members.
items.notes: Signed Nov 5 and reported Nov 6; it does not appear in earlier logs. This resolves the NBP part of W-261105-07. The Bartol and Domański appointments were still pending as of Nov 7, with Tusk saying he expects a quick decision.
